desc:
A monthly ad performance report explains what your advertising spent, what it produced and what to do next, in language an owner can read quickly. Ecom Swift LLC builds the report from your own ad accounts and ends it with clear next steps.

## What is a monthly ad performance report?

A monthly ad performance report is a summary of how your paid campaigns did over one month: what you spent, how many people clicked, how many bought or enquired and what each result cost. A good one also compares the month with the one before and explains the reasons behind any change. Raw platform dashboards show numbers. A report tells you what they mean.

Most advertisers already have the data. The trouble is that it lives in separate tools, uses different names for the same thing and arrives without any explanation. Reading three dashboards and guessing the story is a poor use of an owner's time.

## Why regular reporting improves decisions

Ad results move up and down for ordinary reasons, such as weekends, sale periods and competitors spending more. A single week can mislead you. A monthly view smooths out the noise and shows direction: is cost per sale rising, are returning customers growing, is one channel quietly doing most of the work?

Reporting also creates accountability, whether you manage ads yourself, use a freelancer or work with an agency. A written report with consistent numbers makes it hard for a bad month to hide and easy to see a good change worth repeating.

## What a useful report includes

- Total spend and the results it produced: sales, leads or calls.
- Cost per result, compared with the previous month.
- A split by platform, so you see where money worked hardest.
- The best and worst campaigns or ads, named plainly.
- Results by audience or product where the data allows.
- A blended view of cost per sale across all channels.
- Trend notes in plain words, explaining what likely caused each change.
- A short list of next steps, ranked by importance.
- Notes on anything that might distort the numbers, such as a tracking gap.
- A live dashboard link, for those who prefer to check between reports.

## How we produce it

We connect to your ad accounts as a partner or team member with view-only access where the platform offers it, and read the numbers directly. Where tracking looks doubtful, we say so in the report rather than hiding it. We then write the story: what changed, which choices probably caused it and what to try next.

The Basic package covers one platform and one month, with spend, results and three next steps. Standard widens it to two platforms with best and worst campaigns and more detailed trends. Premium covers up to three platforms, adds a live dashboard, a blended cost view and advice for next month's budget, and ends with a review call. You can also add a one-page executive summary, an extra platform or a second month. Each order is a single report, so there is no automatic renewal, and we can quote a repeat when you want one.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Decide what one good result means before reading the report.
- Compare months of similar length and season.
- Read the next steps first, then the details.
- Keep the same definitions each month, so trends stay honest.
- Share the report with whoever manages your ads.

**Avoid:**
- Judging a campaign on one day of data.
- Mixing results from different attribution settings without noting it.
- Ignoring costs that sit outside the ad platform, such as product cost.
- Treating platform-reported sales as the same as your store's own order count.
- Reacting to every dip with changes that reset learning.

## Who it is for

This service suits an owner who spends on ads but never gets time to read the dashboards. It suits a business paying an outside manager and wanting an independent view of how things are going. It also suits someone preparing for a conversation with a partner, bank or investor.

## What we need and how to start

Send us the platforms you use and the month you want covered, and add us as a partner or team member with view access. Tell us what counts as a result for your business, such as a purchase, a booking or a phone call. If you track profit separately, share the figure so we can factor it in. We never ask for passwords, and we report only on accounts you own.
